experiment: BC6 — optimize the black-copper IR rectenna at realistic ESS temperatures (300-600 C) and compare with a thermoelectric on the same absorbed flux
author_note: 67 C is unrealistic; the ESS interior runs at several hundred C.

model.diode_physics_limit: beta = q / (2 n k T_c), ideality n in {1.0, 1.5} (exponential-diode curvature limit)
model.optimized_variable: diode resistance R on a log grid 10 ohm - 1 Mohm; RC cutoff f_c = 1/(2 pi R C) with roll-off 1/(1+(nu/f_c)^2)
model.validity: square-law regime: V_ac = sqrt(P_in R) <= n k T_c / q; eta_rect = beta^2 P_in R / 4 (so eta_rect <= 1/16 at the validity edge for n = 1)
model.comparison: thermoelectric module on the same net radiative flux: eta_TE = (1 - Tc/Th)(sqrt(1+ZT)-1)/(sqrt(1+ZT)+Tc/Th), ZT = 1 (commercial) and ZT = 0.05 (bulk CuO, from the section 7 correction)

predictions.P1_square_law_ceiling: optimized rectenna efficiency on the net flux stays below 6.25% at every T_h
predictions.P2_500C_output: at 500 C (n = 1, C = 1e-18 F) optimized output >= 100 W/m^2
predictions.P3_TE_wins: a ZT = 1 thermoelectric beats the optimized square-law rectenna at every T_h in 300-600 C
predictions.P4_capacitance: C = 1e-17 F lowers the optimized output by more than 2x relative to 1e-18 F at 500 C
